titre: Antitrust Leniency (1993): Amnesty Reserved for the First to Talk
accroche: On August 10, 1993, the U.S. Justice Department promises amnesty to the first company that reports a cartel: from one application a year to more than one a month.
contenu_vulgarise:
In 1978, the Antitrust Division of the U.S. Department of Justice, the office that criminally prosecutes agreements among competitors, adopts an amnesty policy for companies that report themselves. It is little used: under this regime, the Division receives about one application a year. The text in fact reserved amnesty, at the Division's discretion, for companies that came forward before any investigation had begun.

On August 10, 1993, the Division publishes a revised version. Nine years later, it summarizes the three changes itself: amnesty is automatic if there is no investigation under way; it remains possible when cooperation begins after an investigation has opened; all cooperating officers and employees are protected from criminal prosecution.

## The mechanism

For the company that comes forward before any investigation, the 1993 text sets six conditions, among them: the Division has received no information about the conspiracy from another source, the company has ended its participation, it cooperates fully, and it neither coerced another participant nor led the conspiracy. Amnesty here means not being criminally prosecuted for the facts disclosed.

For the company that does not meet these six conditions, whether it comes forward before or after an investigation opens, seven alternative conditions apply. Two matter more than the others: it must be the first to come forward, and the Division must not yet hold evidence likely to result in a conviction. The decisive word is “first.”

## What the rule produced

On August 10, 1994, the head of the Division, Anne Bingaman, announces that twelve companies have come forward to cooperate since the revision, that is, one a month against one a year under the old policy. In 2002, a Division report finds that the pace exceeds one application a month. It also describes a new situation: companies that come forward within days, sometimes in less than one business day, after an accomplice has taken first place. Only the first to qualify obtains amnesty.

The same report estimates that, in the preceding five years, these applications led to numerous convictions and well over $1.5 billion in fines. In four cases it cites, those of vitamins, graphite electrodes, fine art auctions, and marine construction, the amnesty applicant paid no criminal fine.

## The shift

A cartel rests on trust among competitors: each keeps quiet because each has something to lose. The 1993 rule turns this trust into a race. Since the reward goes only to the first, the danger no longer comes only from the regulator, but from every accomplice who may decide to speak before the others. Compliance that rewards the first to arrive thus moves the risk inside the group.

This text describes the American policy as published on August 10, 1993, and the Division has revised it since. What remains is the question it posed to business criminal law: what is a shared secret worth when the first to break it pays nothing?

repere.texte: Under the old amnesty policy, the Division received about one application a year; under the policy revised in 1993, more than one a month.
repere.source: Antitrust Division, U.S. Department of Justice, Status Report: Corporate Leniency Program, March 7, 2002

carte.punch: Amnesty for the first to report only: from one application a year to one a month.
carte.idee: On August 10, 1993, the U.S. Antitrust Division makes amnesty automatic for the company that reports a cartel before any investigation. Only the first is protected: applications go from about one a year to more than one a month.

quiz.question: Why did the 1993 revision take amnesty applications from one a year to more than one a month?
choix: It made amnesty automatic before any investigation and reserved it for the first, which set off a race
It halved the fines of all companies that acknowledged the cartel
It granted amnesty to each member of the cartel in turn, whatever its order of arrival
It required companies to report themselves on pain of prosecution of their executives
quiz.explication: The gain went only to the first: every accomplice therefore had an interest in speaking before the others. The policy provided neither a halving for everyone, nor amnesty for each regardless of order, nor an obligation to report oneself.

quiz_supplementaire.question: According to the 1978 text, on what basis did the Division grant amnesty before the 1993 revision?
choix: Automatically, as soon as the company ended its participation in the cartel
Only to companies that reimbursed their injured competitors
At the Division's discretion, reserved for companies coming forward before any investigation
To any company among the first two to come forward, whether or not an investigation was open
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The 1978 text reserved amnesty, at the Division's discretion, for companies coming forward before any investigation: automaticity and the possibility of amnesty after an investigation opened came with the 1993 revision.

quiz_supplementaire.question: For a company that does not meet the six conditions of path A, which of the seven alternative conditions matter most?
choix: Having repaid in full the sums collected by the cartel before coming forward
Being the first to come forward, and the Division not yet holding sufficient evidence
Having obtained the prior agreement of the other cartel members to report themselves
Having no executive already criminally prosecuted in another case
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The text says that two conditions matter more than the others among the seven of path B: being the first company to come forward, and the Division not yet holding evidence likely to result in a conviction.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What does the 2002 report observe about the timing of some companies coming forward?
choix: All come forward on the same day, as soon as the 2002 report is published
Most wait until the end of the investigation before coming forward, to limit their risk
They now come forward in alphabetical order to avoid disputes
Some arrive in less than one business day after an accomplice, without obtaining amnesty
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The 2002 report describes companies arriving sometimes in less than one business day after an accomplice has taken first place, without this giving them amnesty: only the first to qualify obtains it.
